summary: Alessandro Giudice works in Indology and linguistics. His posts include Dr. at the University of Munich (attested 2026) and Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Alessandro Graheli specializes in Indology and philosophy. He has held posts as a university assistant at the University of Vienna (attested 2022), principal investigator at the IKGA (attested 2022), and part-time assistant professor at the University of Toronto (attested 2026).

Alex Watson works in Indology and philosophy, having studied at Oxford (BA) and SOAS (MA) under Alexis Sanderson, Harunaga Isaacson, and Ernst Steinkellner. His posts include Harvard Preceptor, Wolfson College fellow (attested 2006), and Ashoka University professor (attested 2020).

Alex Wayman (1921–2004) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. Educated at UCLA, UC Berkeley (PhD), and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Ferdinand Lessing and Murray B. Emeneau, he taught at Wisconsin-Madison (~1961–1967) and Columbia University (1967–1991).

Alexander Berzin (born 1944) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Rutgers, Princeton, and Harvard (PhD under Masatoshi Nagatomi), as well as under traditional teachers including Serkong Rinpoche, he co-founded the LTWA translation bureau (~1972–1979).

Alexander C. McKay (born 1953) is a scholar of Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London in 1995 and held a research fellowship at University College London.

Alexander Coburn Soper (1904–1993) was an art historian of Sinology and Japanology who studied at Hamilton College and Princeton University (PhD 1944). He taught at Bryn Mawr, became a professor at NYU in 1960, and edited Artibus Asiae (1958–1993).

Alexander Cunningham (1814–1893) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under James Prinsep. He founded the Archaeological Survey of India, serving as its first director (1861–1865) and director-general (1871–1885).

Alexander Duff (1806–1878) was a scholar in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of St Andrews (~1821–1829) and the University of Aberdeen, and he taught Krishna Mohan Banerjee.
Alexander Freiman studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (~1903–1907) and Christian Bartholomae (~1907–1908).

Alexander Gardner is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Michigan in 2006 under Donald S. Lopez Jr. He has held a post at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

Alexander Hamilton (1762–1824) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit (1806) and Professor of Sanskrit and Hindu Literature (1808) at the East India Company College.
Alexander James O'Neill specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He pursued PhD studies at the University of Toronto and held a position as a research fellow at Taisho University.

Alexander Johnston (1775–1849) was a historian who studied under Christian Friedrich Schwarz and read law at Göttingen and Lincoln's Inn. He served as chief justice of Ceylon (~1811–1819) and founded the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

Alexander Kabanoff (1952–2000) worked in Japanology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2000, he served as Senior Researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Alexander Kasimovich Kazembek (1802–1870) specialized in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He held academic posts at Kazan Imperial University (~1826–1849) and Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1849–1870).

Alexander Lubotsky (born 1956) is an Indologist, linguist, and Iranianist. After studying at Moscow State University and Leiden University (PhD under Robert S. P. Beekes), he became full professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics at Leiden University in 1999.
Alexander Macmillan is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at SIT Graduate Institute under the advisorship of Elizabeth Morrison (attested 2013).
Alexander Murray (1775–1813) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh from ~1794 to 1806 and later held a post there from ~1812 to 1813.

Alexander Ong Hsu works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2017) supervised by Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer, and held a teaching position at North Dakota State University.
